circulationDisclaimer: 676 individually selectable structures. Lungs and capillary beds are not modeled; educational use only.
circulationDetailsOverview: This separately selectable mesh corresponds to “{{name}}” in the source anatomical atlas.
circulationDetailsLocation: The source identifies it as a {{side}} structure in the {{circuit}} circuit. Its exact position is shown by the selected 3D mesh.
circulationDetailsCaveat: This is an educational anatomical model, not a clinical reference. The source does not include lungs or individually modeled capillary beds.
circulationDetailsReference: Part names and geometry come from the credited Z-Anatomy / BodyParts3D model. Descriptions explain general circulation roles and do not replace clinical references.

circulationFunction.pulmonaryTrunk: Leaves the right ventricle and divides into the pulmonary arteries, carrying oxygen-poor blood toward the lungs.
circulationFunction.pulmonaryArtery: Carries oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle toward the lungs; pulmonary arteries are the exception to the usual oxygen-rich arterial flow.
circulationFunction.pulmonaryVein: Returns oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium; pulmonary veins are the exception to the usual oxygen-poor venous flow.
circulationFunction.aorta: The main systemic artery, carrying oxygen-rich blood from the left ventricle into the body's arterial branches.
circulationFunction.venaCava: Returns systemic venous blood to the right atrium.
circulationFunction.atrium: An atrium receives blood returning to the heart and passes it to a ventricle.
circulationFunction.ventricle: A ventricle pumps blood out of the heart; the right ventricle serves the pulmonary circuit and the left the systemic circuit.
circulationFunction.valve: Heart valves help maintain one-way flow. The precise direction depends on the named valve and its position.
circulationFunction.arteryPulmonary: Carries oxygen-poor blood away from the right side of the heart toward the lungs.
circulationFunction.arterySystemic: Part of the systemic arterial tree. These vessels generally carry oxygen-rich blood from the aorta toward named organs and tissues.
circulationFunction.veinPulmonary: Returns oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium.
circulationFunction.veinSystemic: Returns blood from named organs and tissues toward the right side of the heart.
circulationFunction.coronaryArtery: Supplies oxygen-rich blood to the heart muscle (myocardium). The named coronary artery indicates its branch; individual branching patterns vary.
circulationFunction.coronaryVein: Returns blood from the heart muscle through the coronary veins toward the right atrium, commonly via the coronary sinus.
circulationFunction.heart: Part of the heart's pumping or valve apparatus; the exact role depends on the named structure.
circulationFunction.other: The source classifies this as another cardiovascular structure. Its precise role depends on the anatomical name shown above.

selectCirculationPart: Select a heart or vessel structure on the model
pulmonaryFlow: Right ventricle → pulmonary trunk and arteries → lungs → pulmonary veins → left atrium
systemicFlow: Left ventricle → aorta and arteries → body tissues → veins and venae cavae → right atrium
completeFlow: Pulmonary: heart → lungs → heart. Systemic: heart → body → heart.

helpBody: Rotate with the left mouse button or one finger. Zoom with the wheel or pinch. Pan with the right mouse button or two fingers. Search in English or Arabic, or browse the regions. Selecting a bone focuses the camera and opens its information panel. Press Escape to close the panel. Use the display controls to isolate, separate or reveal the mesh.
sourceGeometry: Original anatomical geometry. Teeth and cartilage are excluded; sternum parts are composed into one adult bone.
